title: The Extraction of the Green Zone Anew
premise: Wendell Zhou, a whistle-blower living under four names, discovers her safe house listed for sale with interior photos that reveal hidden details only her former handlers could know. Realizing the extraction network that trained her has been corrupted and is selling its own assets, she goes on the offensive, hunting the broker behind the listing through a web of dead drops, forged identities, and old debts. As allies from her found family of exiles are picked off one by one, Wendell must decide whether to trust the one person who trained her — the man who taught her to lie. In the end, she burns the network's central archive in a public leak, sacrifices her fourth name to save a young whistle-blower under her protection, and finally lives openly under her real name for the first time in nine years.
about_author: Dominic Galloway is a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing security briefings before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems they helped build.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Bag
chapters.summary: Wendell Zhou's POV. We meet her mid-routine: rehearsing her cover story as 'Mara Voss,' checking the go-bag by the door, memorizing exits. The chapter establishes her discipline and loneliness. Emotional beat: controlled paranoia masking a deep ache for a life she can't have.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A routine identity check turns catastrophic when she finds her safe house on a real estate site — interior photos showing her hidden document cache behind the kitchen panel. Someone photographed her sanctuary without her knowledge. Emotional beat: the floor drops out; invisibility was an illusion.

chapters.title: Protocol Ember
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She executes emergency relocation protocol, contacting 'the Lattice,' the extraction network that trained her, using codes she hasn't needed in years. The response comes back wrong — a phrase retired three years ago. Emotional beat: dawning horror that the network itself is compromised.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Her to Lie
chapters.summary: Dual POV begins with Ilya Brandt, Wendell's former handler, now semi-retired. He receives word that 'assets are being liquidated' and recognizes Wendell's safe house in the listing photos. He burns his own cover to warn her. Emotional beat: guilt and paternal protectiveness entangled with self-interest.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She meets Brandt for the first time in six years. He confirms the Lattice's leadership is selling asset locations to the highest bidder — including the corporations Wendell exposed. Emotional beat: wary reunion; trust extended like a blade held handle-first.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Grey Coat
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Following a lead, she finds Priya Nair, a nineteen-year-old whistle-blower the network abandoned mid-extraction. Wendell recognizes her younger self. She takes Priya in against every rule of tradecraft. Emotional beat: found family igniting against survival instinct.

chapters.title: Photos Tell Lies
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. He analyzes the listing metadata and traces it to a boutique brokerage called Meridian Estates — a shell company. Inside its client files he finds other safe houses listed, each tied to a former Lattice asset. Emotional beat: cold fury hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: What Mara Voss Owes
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. To access Meridian's records she resurrects her second name, 'Elena Marsh,' walking back into a city where people remember her face. An old contact demands a favor in return. Emotional beat: the past as debt collector; every name costs something.

chapters.title: Nine Minutes in the Server Room
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, intercut with Priya keeping watch. Wendell copies Meridian's client ledger during a building evacuation drill. She finds her own file — and a buyer's code name: GREEN ZONE. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into violation; she was inventory.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Short List
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Cross-referencing the ledger, he identifies eleven assets marked for sale and four already extracted — or eliminated. Among them: the couple who hid Wendell after her first leak. Emotional beat: grief as fuel; the body count gives the fight moral weight.

chapters.title: Safe House Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She moves Priya to a fallback location but realizes every option requires routes the Lattice built — meaning routes the enemy knows. She starts building her own network from scratch, recruiting two exiles who owe her. Emotional beat: fragile agency; becoming the handler instead of the handled.

chapters.title: An Old Favor Called In
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (first time). Left alone, Priya panics and contacts a journalist against Wendell's orders, nearly exposing them. Wendell returns to find a surveillance van outside. Emotional beat: friction between protector and protected; trust tested by fear.

chapters.title: Green Zone Identified
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. He decodes the buyer designation: GREEN ZONE is not a corporation but a person — Deputy Director Corliss Hale of the very oversight agency meant to protect whistle-blowers. Emotional beat: betrayal at the institutional level; the shepherd selling the flock.

chapters.title: The Trap They Built for Her
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A message arrives offering Wendell full immunity if she surrenders her evidence — signed by Hale herself. Wendell recognizes the offer as confirmation they know exactly who she is. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into clarity; they've shown their hand.

chapters.title: Burning the Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She stages her own capture as 'Mara Voss,' letting Hale's team take the bait while Priya and the exiles relocate the archive. The plan works, but a sniper's near-miss wounds her escort. Emotional beat: sacrifice with teeth; names are armor until they're targets.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Held in a black site, Wendell plays the frightened accountant while feeding Hale disinformation. Brandt works the outside angle, pressuring Meridian's broker to flip. Emotional beat: performance under pressure; the liar's art as survival.

chapters.title: The Broker Turns
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The Meridian broker, facing exposure, hands over Hale's direct communications — proof of eleven sales and four deaths. Brandt transmits everything to Wendell's dead drop. Emotional beat: small betrayals toppling great ones; corruption devours its own.

chapters.title: Extraction, Reversed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Using protocols only she and Brandt know, Wendell escapes the black site during a prisoner transfer — turning the network's training against the institution that corrupted it. Emotional beat: liberation and rage fused; she was always more than their product.

chapters.title: Everything in the Open
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. From a borrowed newsroom, Priya publishes the full archive — Hale's sales, the black sites, the sold whistle-blowers — with Wendell's testimony attached. The story detonates across every feed. Emotional beat: catharsis; silence broken at last.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Exit
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Hale attempts to flee using a Lattice extraction route, but Wendell anticipated it. Confronted at a private airfield, Hale offers Brandt a partnership; he refuses and records her confession. Arrest follows. Emotional beat: power unmasked as cowardice.

chapters.title: The Cost Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Aftermath: hearings begin, the Lattice is dismantled and rebuilt with new safeguards, and Wendell mourns the friends who didn't survive. Brandt asks what she'll do now. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude sharing a table; survival redefined as more than escape.

chapters.title: One Name, Packed Light
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, closing. Wendell unpacks the go-bag for the first time in nine years, signs a lease under her real name, and takes Priya to dinner as family, not assignment. The final image: her door, unlocked. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; visibility chosen, not imposed.
